short: LRS2-BBC outlasts the models: the CTC vs seq2seq comparison is confounded, the 22-point gain is not attributable to the new architecture, and test speaker overlap is unreported.
position: This paper changed two components. Its CTC vs seq2seq study on one Transformer encoder (M06) is standard: the group's concurrent paper had already compared CTC with a Transformer on LRS2, it mixes loss with beam, LM weight and fusion, and the field now trains both jointly. Its lasting contribution, the public LRS2-BBC set (M11), is not reported where it matters: speaker overlap is absent and the group's LRS3 paper says the same people likely recur. The "over 22%" gain is not attributable to the new front-end and back-end (§1): front-end, non-public MV-LRS pretraining and back-end changed together, the 70.4% baseline has no stated decoding conditions, and over the group's own Transformer (50.0%) the paper adds 1.7 points. Video helping clean audio is supported; a CTC vs seq2seq difference on clean audio-visual input (8.2% vs 8.5%) is not, and the noise advantage rests on one matched noise type.
